findings.summary: The title, summary and criterion texts reach main's commit history and the PR title. After the change nothing scans them, and the plan's backstops do not cover this path.
findings.evidence: Read in close.rs: the landing message is `message(&ctx.reading.title, &body, ...)` and `landing_body` starts with `reading.summary.trim()`, then lists each criterion `c.criterion`. run/mod.rs:1426 passes `ctx.reading.title` to `early_pr`, which becomes the PR title. The host squash-merges, so this text becomes the commit on main, and HISTORY.txt shows such subjects. Grep found no `boundary_scan` or `plain_boundary_text` call in close.rs or on the PR title. The policy scan (xtask/tests/policy.rs) checks tracked files, not commit messages, and the writer's scan (D73) covers only what the producer writes. Today the reading check is the only gate keeping a boundary word out of these. The plan's risk mitigation says the writer's scan and the policy scan cover the title or summary path, but neither does. The request assumes the check guards only tracked files, and that premise misses this path. The root-cause default asks the plan to name it. Fix: The request requires a summary holding a word to be accepted, so keep the narrowing and close the leak where Athena writes the text. Run the title through `athena_context::briefs::plain_boundary_text` (it exists for 'text that Athena itself writes') in `message`/`closing_subject` and for the `early_pr` title. Do the same for the body from `landing_body`. Add a unit test showing a reading whose title and summary hold a boundary word yields a landing message and PR title that pass `boundary_scan`. That widens the scope to run/close.rs (and run/mod.rs), so list them as departures. If the planner judges that too wide, the plan must at least drop the false backstop claim, state the gap in D153's Tradeoff and the module docs, and raise it as an open question for the user, not leave it implied as covered.

findings.summary: The scope of the two departures (run_pin_tests.rs, refusal_corpus.rs) is justified. Athena flagged them; they are test-only and needed.
findings.evidence: Read run_pin_tests.rs:1718: the end-to-end test asserts a summary refusal and would fail criterion 5 if left as it is. refusal_corpus.rs INPUT_FORMS has 16 entries and no boundary-word case, so the corpus could not show the narrowing. Fix: No change needed beyond naming them as departures in the change description, as the plan already does.

findings.summary: The refusal-corpus source strings for the new cases should follow the existing 'job <id>, ...; rebuilt from the job brief' pattern, or say plainly that the cases come from the request.
findings.evidence: Existing cases in refusal_corpus.rs (lines 492, 512) name a job id and 'rebuilt from the job brief'. Step 9's source cites dates, not job ids, because the records are absent. Fix: Write the source as 'request of job 20261031-215030-b0nv citing refusals on 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-30; rebuilt from the request'.

summary: The plan matches the request and the reading, and the code it names checks out. `reading_text_fields` is at reading.rs:2709 and `check_boundary_and_repo_files` at :2771. The test fixtures exist, and `governed_reading` builds Content-kind criteria. The corpus harness, INPUT_FORMS[16] and `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` exist, and the run_pin_tests.rs:1718 test exists. The demonstrations exercise the real entry points (`check_reading_acceptance`, `Athena::ask`, the corpus harness), and each would fail under the old scan. One soundness problem stands. The reading's title becomes the squash-merge commit subject and the PR title, and its summary and criterion texts become the commit body (close.rs:117, :590-591; run/mod.rs:1426). Nothing rewords or scans that text before it reaches main's history. The plan's risk mitigation names the writer's scan and the policy scan as backstops, but neither covers commit messages. Today the reading check is the only gate on this path, so the narrowing opens a leak the plan claims is covered. The fix is to apply the existing `plain_boundary_text` where Athena composes the landing message and PR title, with a test. At minimum the plan must record the gap honestly and raise it with the user. The criterion-kind proxy for 'text to write into a file' is imperfect, but the plan states both edge cases and the user accepted it, so it is not a finding.
